# FlowPanel

> A typed admin panel for Next.js. Describe your Drizzle or Prisma tables in a typed config and get lists, forms, record pages and dashboards at /admin. Open source, MIT licensed.
> Admin panel for Next.js in one package: config builders, Drizzle and Prisma adapters, the App Router runtime, React UI and auth presets.

```bash
pnpm dlx @flowpanel/cli init
pnpm dev
```

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs · Source: https://github.com/getflowpanel/flowpanel

Generated from the reference documentation. Property tables come from the
packages' own TypeScript declarations. Code blocks are excerpts from that
documentation: blocks the docs mark `twoslash` are type-checked in CI,
`excerpt` blocks are illustrative and may omit surrounding code.

## defineAdmin

The config entry point and every option it accepts.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/define-config

Documented types: defineAdmin, AdminDefinition, AuthConfig, ThemeConfig, ShellConfig, AuditConfig, AuditEvent, SecurityConfig, PluralLabel, LabelsConfig, CommandPaletteConfig, CommandGroup, CommandItem, ResolvedAdminConfig

`defineAdmin` takes the config object, validates it, fills defaults, and returns
the `ResolvedAdminConfig` that `createFlowpanel` serves. It does no I/O, so a page,
script or test can import the config freely.

### AdminDefinition

`adapter` and `auth` are required. Without the rest you get no resources, the
sidebar shell, English labels, no audit sink, in-process realtime and no rate limit.

`AdminDefinition`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id?` | `string` | Stable id surfaced in the wire client metadata (`client.id`, default `"local"`) to tell multi-admin deployments apart. |
| `adapter` | `Adapter` | Database binding — `drizzleAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or your own. |
| `auth` | `AuthConfig` | How the admin reads sessions and roles. |
| `scope?` | `(ctx: ScopeContext) => Promise<Scope> \| Scope` | Tenant scope resolved per request, then applied to every query. |
| `theme?` | `ThemeConfig` | Branding, color scheme, design tokens and component overrides. |
| `shell?` | `ShellConfig \| ShellMode` | Chrome around the content area — sidebar, tabs, or none. |
| `labels?` | `LabelsConfig` | Override built-in UI strings. |
| `formatting?` | `FormattingConfig` | Locale, timezone and currency for numbers, money and timestamps. |
| `resources?` | `Resources` | Tables the admin manages. |
| `dashboards?` | `DashboardConfig[]` | Widget dashboards. |
| `pages?` | `PageConfig[]` | Custom pages rendered inside the shell. |
| `queues?` | `QueueConfig[]` | BullMQ queues surfaced in the admin. |
| `commandPalette?` | `CommandPaletteConfig` | What ⌘K offers. |
| `audit?` | `AuditConfig` | Audit trail for every mutation. |
| `realtime?` | `RealtimeConfig` | Cross-instance realtime transport. Redis in production. |
| `rateLimit?` | `RateLimitConfig` | Throttle requests per user or per IP. |
| `security?` | `SecurityConfig` | Browser request protections. Same-origin mutation checks are enabled by default. |
| `readOnly?` | `boolean` | Put the whole admin in read-only mode. |
| `paths?` | `AdminPathsInput` | Mount points for the generated admin UI and HTTP API. |
| `hooks?` | `{ onError?: (err: Error, ctx: ErrorContext) => void \| Promise<void>; }` | Cross-cutting callbacks. |

### AuthConfig

`session` and `role` run on every request, so keep them cheap. `session` receives
the request being served.

`AuthConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `(req: Request) => Promise<Session \| null>` | Reads the current session. Called on every request and page render, handed the request being served. Lets a provider inspect headers, cookies or the host without forging one. |
| `role` | `(session: Session \| null) => string \| Promise<string>` | Maps a session to a role string, which every `requireRole` gate compares against. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[] \| ((s: Session \| null) => boolean)` | Admin-wide gate. Blocks every route and page before anything else runs. |
| `signInUrl?` | `string` | Where to send an unauthenticated visitor. Without it they get an inline notice. |
| `forbiddenUrl?` | `string` | Where to send a signed-in visitor who lacks the role. |
| `userId?` | `(session: Session \| null) => string \| null` | Extracts the actor id for audit rows and per-user rate limiting. |
| `allowUnauthenticated?` | `boolean` | Declares this admin reachable without a role gate — fronted by a VPN or authenticating proxy instead. Production refuses to start without `requireRole` unless this is `true` AND the admin is `readOnly`. |

`requireRole` is the admin-wide gate. A config with no `requireRole`, no resource
`access` and no global `scope` serves every page to anonymous visitors, and `defineAdmin` warns
in development; `allowUnauthenticated: true` marks that as intended. In
production, a config without `auth.requireRole` refuses to start unless it sets
both `allowUnauthenticated: true` and `readOnly: true`.

The presets `withBetterAuth`, `withClerk`, `withNextAuth`, `withLucia` and
`devAuth`, imported from `@flowpanel/kit/auth`, build an `AuthConfig`; see [Authentication](/docs/guides/authentication).

### ThemeConfig

`ThemeConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand?` | `{ name?: string; logo?: string; href?: string }` | Product name, logo and home link shown in the shell header. |
| `accent?` | `string` | Accent color as an HSL triplet, e.g. `"220 90% 50%"`. An `hsl(…)` wrapper is unwrapped. Data fills take it too unless `cssVars` sets `--fp-data`. |
| `accentDark?` | `string` | Dark-mode accent override, same format as `accent`; a light-tuned accent usually fails WCAG contrast on dark. Dark data fills take it too unless `cssVarsDark` sets `--fp-data`. |
| `mode?` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto"` | Initial color scheme. `"auto"` follows the operating system. |
| `cssVars?` | `ThemeTokens` | Override any `--fp-*` design token, e.g. `{ "--fp-radius": "0.25rem" }`. |
| `cssVarsDark?` | `ThemeTokens` | Dark-mode token overrides, scoped to FlowPanel's dark roots and portals. Choose foreground tokens for contrast against the actual dark background. |
| `components?` | `Partial<FlowpanelComponentSlots>` | Replace built-in components. See the styling guide. |
| `user?` | `(s: Session \| null) => \| { name?: string; email?: string; avatar?: string; items?: Array<{ label: string; href?: string; variant?: "default" \| "destructive" }>; signOut?: string; } \| undefined` | What the account menu shows for the current session. Return `undefined` to render no menu at all — the usual choice when there is no session. |

`components` is `Partial<FlowpanelComponentSlots>`; see
[theme slots](/docs/customization/styling#replace-a-shared-component).

`accent` and `cssVars` apply to `[data-flowpanel-root]` and
`[data-flowpanel-portal]` only, so the host's tokens are untouched.
`accentDark` and `cssVarsDark` apply in dark mode. Every `--fp-*` token can be
overridden:

```ts excerpt
theme: {
  brand: { name: "Acme", logo: "/logo.svg", href: "/" },
  accent: "262 83% 58%",
  accentDark: "262 90% 72%",
  cssVars: { "--fp-radius": "0.25rem" },
  cssVarsDark: { "--fp-text-1": "0 0% 98%" },
}
```

Colours are HSL triplets. `accent` and `accentDark` may also be written as `hsl(...)`, and the wrapper is removed for you; `cssVars` and `cssVarsDark` are written as given.

`user` fills the account menu at the foot of the sidebar, or the end of the tab
strip. Return nothing and no menu renders:

```ts excerpt
theme: {
  user: (session) => ({
    name: session?.user?.name,
    email: session?.user?.email,
    avatar: session?.user?.image,
    items: [{ label: "Settings", href: "/settings" }],
    signOut: "/api/auth/signout",
  }),
}
```

### ShellConfig

`shell: "tabs"` is shorthand for `shell: { mode: "tabs" }`.

`ShellConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode?` | `ShellMode` |  |
| `brand?` | `{ name?: string; logo?: string; href?: string } \| false` | Overrides `theme.brand`. `false` hides brand even in sidebar/tabs. |
| `skipLink?` | `boolean` | Disable when the host application layout already renders a skip-to-content link. |

`ShellMode` is `"sidebar" | "tabs" | "bare"`:

- `"sidebar"`: left navigation and brand. The default.
- `"tabs"`: a tab strip above the content, for an admin under the host's own header.
- `"bare"`: no chrome; your layout supplies it. Toasts, the drawer, the command
  palette and realtime still mount.

`skipLink: false` removes the skip-to-content link when the host layout already
renders one.

#### Navigation groups

`navGroup` on a dashboard, page, resource or queue moves its entry from its kind's
group into a named one. Groups appear in the order of their first entry. A
`{ label, collapsed: true }` group stays folded until it holds the current page.

```ts excerpt
const journals = { label: "Journals", collapsed: true } as const;

resource(schema.scraperRun, { plural: "Scraper runs", navGroup: journals });
resource(schema.aiRun, { plural: "AI runs", navGroup: journals });
resource(schema.category, { plural: "Categories", navGroup: "Reference data" });
```

With `shell: "tabs"` the groups flatten into one row of tabs, so a group's label
and `collapsed` do not show there.

### AuditConfig

`AuditConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled?` | `boolean` | Turn auditing on. Individual resources can opt out with `audit: false`. |
| `sink?` | `(event: AuditEvent) => Promise<void>` | Where events go — your table, your log pipeline, anywhere. |

#### AuditEvent

What `audit.sink` receives. FlowPanel stores no audit rows itself.

`AuditEvent`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Who acted, from `AuthConfig.userId`. Null when unresolvable. |
| `action` | `string` | What ran, e.g. `"orders.action.refund"` or `"orders.inline-update"`. |
| `resource?` | `string` | Resource name the action targeted. |
| `targetId?` | `string` | Id of the affected row. Bulk actions carry the first ten, comma-joined. |
| `diff?` | `{ before: unknown; after: unknown }` | Before/after values, for mutations that can compute them. |
| `ip?` | `string` |  |
| `userAgent?` | `string` |  |
| `at` | `Date` |  |

### SecurityConfig

Cross-origin writes are blocked by default. `trustedOrigins` allows exact
origins. Requests without browser `Origin` or Fetch Metadata headers, such as
server-to-server calls, pass this check.

`SecurityConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sameOrigin?` | `boolean` | Reject cross-origin write requests using Origin and Fetch Metadata headers. Enabled by default. Disable only when an upstream gateway enforces an equivalent policy. |
| `trustedOrigins?` | `string[]` | Additional exact origins allowed to submit writes, for example `https://ops.example.com`. |

### RateLimitConfig

`RateLimitConfig` is `RateLimitOptions` plus `per` (`"user"` or `"ip"`,
defaulting to `"user"`) and `enabled`.

```ts excerpt
type RateLimitOptions =
  | { driver: "memory"; limit: number; windowMs: number }
  | { driver: "redis"; url: string; limit: number; windowMs: number; keyPrefix?: string };
```

The memory driver counts per process; use Redis with more than one instance. A
caller over the limit gets `429`.

### RealtimeConfig

An alias of `PublisherOptions`. Without it, events reach only the process that
published them. See [Realtime](/docs/guides/realtime).

### LabelsConfig

Text for the built-in UI. Groups merge over the English defaults; an undefined
value keeps its default and an empty string is used as given. A component's own
placeholder or label prop wins.

`pagination.page`, `pagination.pageSize` and `bulkBar.selected` take `{n}`.

`plurals` holds count templates for languages whose count words change with the
number: a `PluralLabel` has one template per `Intl.PluralRules` category of
`formatting.locale`, with `other` as the fallback. `plurals.results` wins over
`table.result` and `table.results`, and `plurals.selected` over `bulkBar.selected`:

```ts excerpt
labels: {
  plurals: {
    results: { one: "{n} запись", few: "{n} записи", many: "{n} записей", other: "{n} записи" },
    selected: { one: "Выбрана {n}", few: "Выбраны {n}", other: "Выбрано {n}" },
  },
},
```

`formatCount(label, count, locale)` from `@flowpanel/kit` picks the form in your
own server code. A preset's plural gives way to a string template you set
for the same count.

`PluralLabel`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zero?` | `string` |  |
| `one?` | `string` |  |
| `two?` | `string` |  |
| `few?` | `string` |  |
| `many?` | `string` |  |
| `other` | `string` |  |

`dateRange.locale` sets the calendar and count formatting, falling back to
`en-US`. `form.createTitle` and `form.editTitle` take `{label}`. `access` holds the
sign-in and access-denied screens shown when `auth.signInUrl` or
`auth.forbiddenUrl` is not set.

A Russian `formatting.locale` (`"ru"`, `"ru-RU"`) makes `RU_LABELS` the base that
`labels` merges over, so set only the strings you want different, such as
`labels: { actions: { new: "Добавить" } }`. Other locales use English. Import
`RU_LABELS` or `DEFAULT_LABELS` from `@flowpanel/kit`; `labels: DEFAULT_LABELS`
keeps English under a Russian locale.

`LabelsConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noResults?` | `string` | Empty list state — used when a resource list returns 0 rows. |
| `allOption?` | `string` | Empty filter / select dropdown — the "any/all" sentinel. |
| `navigation?` | `{ skipToContent?: string; admin?: string; open?: string; title?: string; accountMenu?: string; account?: string; signOut?: string; scrollHint?: string; dashboards?: string; resources?: string; pages?: string; queues?: string; theme?: string; toggleTheme?: string; }` |  |
| `table?` | `{ /** Templates use `{n}`. Separate one/many templates avoid English suffixes. */ result?: string; results?: string; actions?: string; rowActions?: string; rowsHint?: string; rowsReadOnlyHint?: string; selectRow?: string; selectAll?: string; deselectAll?: string; /** Title of a list with no rows and no `emptyState`. Use `{label}` for the plural label. */ empty?: string; /** The pencil on an editable cell. Use `{label}` for the column label. */ editCell?: string; /** After an editable cell saves. */ saved?: string; }` |  |
| `dateRange?` | `{ /** Locale for calendar presentation; identical during SSR and hydration. */ locale?: string; label?: string; fieldLabel?: string; any?: string; clear?: string; clearAction?: string; from?: string; until?: string; previousMonth?: string; nextMonth?: string; firstMonth?: string; secondMonth?: string; pickEnd?: string; noSelection?: string; today?: string; yesterday?: string; last7d?: string; last30d?: string; thisMonth?: string; lastMonth?: string; MTD?: string; QTD?: string; YTD?: string; }` |  |
| `savedViews?` | `{ save?: string; saveTrigger?: string; name?: string; current?: string; label?: string; yours?: string; saveCurrent?: string; saved?: string; deleted?: string; delete?: string; storageError?: string; }` |  |
| `pagination?` | `{ label?: string; previous?: string; next?: string; of?: string; rowsPerPage?: string; /** Accessible page button name. Use `{n}` for the page number. */ page?: string; /** Page-size option. Use `{n}` for the row count. */ pageSize?: string; }` | Pagination chrome. |
| `filters?` | `{ label?: string; clear?: string; yes?: string; no?: string; searchPlaceholder?: string; }` |  |
| `bulkBar?` | `{ /** Use `{n}` for the selection count. Default: `"{n} selected"`. */ selected?: string; clear?: string; }` | Bulk action bar. |
| `plurals?` | `{ /** The table's row count, every count `1` included. */ results?: PluralLabel; /** The bulk bar's and a multi-select filter's selection count. */ selected?: PluralLabel; /** A timeline day's event count; wins over `timeline.event`/`timeline.events`. */ events?: PluralLabel; }` | Count templates per `Intl.PluralRules` category; when set, they win over `table.result`/`results` and `bulkBar.selected`. |
| `searchPlaceholder?` | `string` | Resource search input placeholder. Use `{label}` for the resource's label. |
| `actions?` | `{ edit?: string; save?: string; cancel?: string; delete?: string; restore?: string; new?: string; create?: string; export?: string; import?: string; }` | Generic action buttons. |
| `form?` | `{ /** Edit page heading. Use `{label}` for the resource's singular label. */ editTitle?: string; /** Create page heading. Use `{label}` for the resource's singular label. */ createTitle?: string; /** The empty choice in a select control. */ selectPlaceholder?: string; /** A reference search with nothing to offer. */ noOptions?: string; /** A reference search still in flight. */ searching?: string; /** A reference search that failed. */ loadFailed?: string; /** An empty value the write needs. Use `{label}` for the field's label. */ required?: string; /** A value that is not a number. Use `{label}`. */ invalidNumber?: string; /** A value that is neither true nor false. Use `{label}`. */ invalidBoolean?: string; /** A value that is not a date. Use `{label}`. */ invalidDate?: string; /** A value a unique column already holds. Use `{label}`. */ taken?: string; /** A unique violation the database did not tie to one column. */ conflict?: string; /** A reference to a row that does not exist. Use `{label}`. */ missingReference?: string; /** A foreign key violation the database did not tie to one column. */ missingLink?: string; /** A delete that other rows still reference. */ inUse?: string; /** The create page of a resource with `create.disabled`. */ createDisabled?: string; /** The edit page of a resource with `update.disabled`. */ editDisabled?: string; }` | Generated create and edit form chrome. |
| `drawer?` | `{ close?: string; viewDetails?: string; /** While the record loads. */ loading?: string; /** A resource tab with no rows. Use `{resource}`. */ noRows?: string; /** A widgets tab that declares none. */ noWidgets?: string; /** A chart, which only a dashboard or a record page draws. Use `{n}` for its points. */ chartElsewhere?: string; /** A widget kind a drawer does not draw. Use `{kind}`. */ unsupported?: string; /** The dialog's name before the record loads. */ title?: string; /** The record could not be loaded. */ loadFailed?: string; }` | Drawer chrome. |
| `detail?` | `{ /** A fields tab with nothing the reader is allowed to see. */ noFields?: string; /** A tab naming a resource that is not registered. Use `{resource}`. */ unknownResource?: string; /** A counted tab's label. Use `{label}` and `{count}`. */ tabCount?: string; }` | Full-page detail chrome. |
| `related?` | `{ /** Link from a related tab to the target resource's own list. */ openList?: string; }` | Related detail-tab chrome. |
| `notFound?` | `{ title?: string; description?: string; back?: string; }` | The admin's own not-found page, for a URL no resource or dashboard matches. |
| `access?` | `{ /** No session: the reader has to sign in. */ signInTitle?: string; signInDescription?: string; /** A session whose role the admin does not allow. */ deniedTitle?: string; deniedDescription?: string; }` | The screens shown in place of the admin when `auth.signInUrl` or `auth.forbiddenUrl` is not set. |
| `formError?` | `string` | Form-level banner shown when a submit fails with no field errors of its own. |
| `confirm?` | `{ title?: string; ok?: string; cancel?: string; }` | Confirm dialog. |
| `widget?` | `WidgetLabels` | Dashboard and detail-tab widget chrome. |
| `timeline?` | `TimelineLabels` | `timeline()` chrome. |
| `heatmap?` | `HeatmapLabels` | `heatmap()` chrome. |
| `checklist?` | `ChecklistLabels` | `checklist()` chrome. |
| `errors?` | `{ /** Failed page read. Use `{resource}` and `{operation}`. */ queryTitle?: string; /** What to check after a failed page read. */ queryHint?: string; /** What to check when the database refused the connection or could not be reached. */ connectionHint?: string; /** Correlation line tying the card to the server log. Use `{id}`. */ requestId?: string; /** Failed widget, shown in the widget's own frame. */ widgetTitle?: string; widgetHint?: string; /** Button that re-runs a failed widget. */ retry?: string; /** Disclosure holding the error's own message, outside production only. */ details?: string; }` | FlowPanel's own failure surfaces, shown in place of the data that did not load. |
| `palette?` | `{ placeholder?: string; noResults?: string; title?: string; description?: string; loading?: string; }` | ⌘K palette. |

### CommandPaletteConfig

`CommandPaletteConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groups?` | `CommandGroup[]` | Your own groups, listed after the built-in ones. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | Placeholder text for the input. Defaults to `labels.palette.placeholder`. Default: `"Search resources, actions…"`. |
| `disableNavigation?` | `boolean` | Drop the built-in group that links to every resource. |
| `disableTheme?` | `boolean` | Drop the built-in light/dark toggle. |

#### CommandGroup

`CommandGroup`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `items` | `CommandItem[]` |  |

#### CommandItem

`CommandItem`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `shortcut?` | `string` | Shortcut hint shown on the right, e.g. `"⌘J"`. Display only — bind it yourself. |
| `keywords?` | `string[]` | Extra terms that should match this item in search. |
| `action` | `{ type: "navigate"; href: string }` | What running the item does. Only `navigate` is supported. |

`CommandItem.icon` uses the same `IconName` registry as resources and actions;
see [resource icons](/docs/reference/resources#icons).

### ResolvedAdminConfig

What `defineAdmin` returns.

`ResolvedAdminConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__resolved` | `true` |  |
| `resources` | `Resources` |  |
| `resourcesByName` | `Map<string, ResourceConfig>` |  |
| `dashboardsByPath` | `Map<string, DashboardConfig>` |  |
| `pagesByPath` | `Map<string, PageConfig>` |  |
| `queuesByKey` | `Map<string, QueueConfig>` |  |
| `paths` | `AdminPaths` | Normalized mount points with leading slashes and no trailing slash. |
| `warnings` | `readonly string[]` | Config problems that do not stop the admin from booting. `flowpanel doctor` prints them; development prints each once. |

`defineAdmin` throws if two resources share a name, two dashboards or pages
share a path, or two queues share a key.

It also throws when a config points at a resource name nothing resolves to:
`reference.resource` on a column or field, a drawer or detail tab's `resource`,
or a `table()` widget's `resource`. The names it checks against are the
*resolved* ones, so a Drizzle table declared as `pgTable("ai_usage", …)` is
`"ai_usage"` even when the exported variable is `aiUsage`. The error names the
config path and suggests the near match.

Bind the definition with `createFlowpanel(config)`, then mount its page and
handlers. The runtime comes from `@flowpanel/kit/next`:

```ts excerpt
// app/admin/[[...slug]]/page.tsx
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "@/flowpanel.config";

const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);

export default flowpanel.page;
```

```ts excerpt
// app/api/flowpanel/[...route]/route.ts
import { createFlowpanel } from "@flowpanel/kit/next";
import config from "@/flowpanel.config";

const flowpanel = createFlowpanel(config);

export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } = flowpanel.handlers;
```

### Default bulk delete

When a resource has delete enabled and declares no `bulkActions`, `defineAdmin`
injects a default `delete` bulk action. Set `delete.confirm` to replace its confirmation description. Opt out
with `bulkActions: []` or `delete: { disabled: true }`.

`readOnly: true` short-circuits the whole rule: a read-only admin rewrites
every resource to `bulkActions: []` (and empties `actions` and the drawer's
actions, disables create/update/delete, drops `import`, and clears every
column's `editable`), so no default delete is injected for any resource.

### Reserved names

`defineAdmin` throws when a resource name or queue key is `dashboards`, `drawer`
or `queues`: the admin's own routes use those URL segments. Change `options.name`
on the resource or `options.key` on the queue.

### Behavior beyond validation

1. **Fills `columns`** from `adapter.introspect(ref)` for any resource that
   omitted them, in introspection order. If the adapter cannot introspect the
   ref, or reports zero columns, that throws.
2. **Injects the default bulk delete** (above).
3. **Normalizes `paths.admin`** and every dashboard and page `path`: a missing
   leading `/` is added, a trailing one stripped.

`introspect` reads the table object or DMMF; it does not query the database.

#### `paths` and a Next.js deployment `basePath`

`paths.admin` and `paths.api` are app-relative: they say where the admin sits inside
your app, not where the app sits under a domain. If `next.config` sets its own
`basePath`, leave both alone. Next serves and links everything under that prefix
already.

FlowPanel adds the deployment prefix for you to the requests the browser issues
by itself: the client fetches built from `paths.api`, the generated form actions
and the SSE endpoint. `Link`, router navigation and `revalidatePath` are prefixed
by Next and are left untouched. Only a fetch you write yourself in a client
component against `paths.api` needs the helper. Server code calls the runtime
through `createFlowpanel(config).request()` instead of fetching its own routes.

```ts excerpt
import { withDeploymentBasePath } from "@flowpanel/kit/react";

await fetch(`${withDeploymentBasePath(config.paths.api)}/user/u1/actions/verify`, {
  method: "POST",
});
```

#### Formatting

`formatting` decides how the admin renders values, on the server and in the
browser alike:

```ts excerpt
formatting: { locale: "ru-RU", timeZone: "Europe/Moscow", currency: "RUB" },
```

`locale` governs the `number` and `money` column formats and the date shape;
`currency` is the default for a `money` column that names none, and a column's own
`currency` still wins. A set `timeZone` is the one clock of the admin: server
strings, chart ticks and every `LocalTime` render in it, before and after
hydration. Left unset, the server and the first paint use UTC and a `LocalTime`
switches to the reader's own zone after hydration. A `LocalTime` given its own
`fallbackTimeZone` keeps that switch either way.

With no `locale`, dates print as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` and numbers use `en-US` grouping.

#### Identifiers in URLs

Record identifiers are percent-encoded into the URL and decoded once when the page
route reads them back, so an id containing `/`, `%`, `?`, `#` or a space addresses
the record it names. Configured dashboard and page paths keep their separators:
`/reports/weekly` stays two segments.

A row whose projection did not include the key column is displayed but not treated
as addressable: no selection, no inline editing, no row activation. Keep the key
column in `columns`, or in `detail.tabs[].fields`, wherever the table has to act
on rows.

## resource()

Every option on a resource, its columns, fields and filters.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/resources

Documented types: resource, ResourceOptions, ColumnDef, formatColumnValue, formatNumber, enumOf, EnumDef, FieldDef, FilterDef, DetailOptions, DetailHeaderContext, DetailBadge, related, RelatedOptions, DetailTab, DetailTabContext, ListResult, ResourceConfig

`ref` is a Drizzle table or a Prisma model name. The row type comes from
[`InferRow<Ref>`](/docs/reference/registry#inferrow), which types `columns`,
`search`, `filters` and `defaultSort`.

```ts excerpt
import { resource } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { orders } from "@/db/schema";

export const ordersResource = resource(orders, {
  label: "Order",
  plural: "Orders",
  icon: "shopping-cart",
  columns: ["id", "customerEmail", { field: "total", format: "money" }, "status"],
  search: ["customerEmail"],
  filters: ["status", { field: "createdAt", type: "daterange" }],
  defaultSort: { field: "createdAt", dir: "desc" },
  detail: { title: (row) => `Order · ${row.customerEmail}` },
});
```

### ResourceOptions

`ResourceOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name?` | `string` | URL segment and registry key. Defaults to the adapter's table name. |
| `label?` | `string` | Singular label shown in headings and buttons. |
| `labelOne?` | `string` | Label for exactly one row, e.g. `"Customer"`, used in record, create and edit titles. Falls back to `label`, then the resource name made singular: `order_items` reads "Order item". |
| `plural?` | `string` | Plural label shown in the nav and list title. |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered in navigation and the command palette. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Keep the resource out of the navigation — its routes still work. |
| `navGroup?` | `NavGroupRef` | Sidebar group for this resource. Default: the Resources group. |
| `expose?` | `(keyof Row & string)[]` | Additional fields shared by list and detail presentation. Declare render dependencies explicitly; callbacks never receive an undeclared DB row. |
| `columns?` | `(keyof Row \| ColumnDef<Row>)[]` | Columns of the list table, in order; a bare string is a field name. Omitted, `defineAdmin` fills it in introspection order. |
| `search?` | `(keyof Row & string)[]` | Fields the search box queries. Without this, search is disabled. |
| `filters?` | `(keyof Row \| FilterDef<Row>)[]` | Filter controls above the list. A bare string always renders a text filter — declare a `FilterDef` for any other control. |
| `defaultSort?` | `{ field: keyof Row & string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }` | Sort applied when the URL carries none. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Rows per page. Default: `20`. |
| `density?` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | Row height preset for the list table. Default: `"comfortable"`. |
| `rowClick?` | `"detail" \| "drawer" \| false` | What a row click — and Enter on the focused row — does. A row the projection cannot identify never acts. Default: ``"drawer"` when `drawer` is configured, otherwise `"detail"``. |
| `rowKey?` | `keyof Row & string` | Property holding each row's unique id. Default: `"id"`. |
| `drawer?` | `DrawerConfig<Row>` | Side panel opened for a single row. |
| `detail?` | `DetailOptions<Row>` | Full-page view at `<paths.admin>/<resource>/<id>`. |
| `schema?` | `z.ZodTypeAny \| { create?: z.ZodTypeAny; update?: z.ZodTypeAny }` | Validation for writes. Overrides the schema inferred from the adapter. |
| `writeTo?` | `unknown` | The table that create, update, delete and restore write to, when the resource reads a view. Omitted on a view: the resource is read-only, and a declared create/update/delete/import is an error at `defineAdmin`. |
| `create?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; fields?: FieldDef<Row>[]; defaultValues?: Partial<Row> }` | Create form. `disabled` removes the route, not just the button. |
| `update?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; fields?: FieldDef<Row>[]; /** Additional readable values available to edit-form hidden/readOnly predicates; never a control, default or write. */ expose?: (keyof Row & string)[]; /** * How the record page's edit button reads: `"primary"` fills it with the accent. * @defaultValue "secondary" */ emphasis?: ActionEmphasis; }` | Edit form. `disabled` removes the route, not just the button. |
| `delete?` | `{ disabled?: boolean; softDelete?: keyof Row & string; confirm?: string }` | Delete behaviour. Set `softDelete` to a timestamp column to keep rows recoverable. |
| `actions?` | `RowAction<Row, any, any>[]` | Per-row actions, rendered inline or in the row's menu. |
| `bulkActions?` | `BulkAction<Row, any, any>[]` | Actions applied to a selection of rows. |
| `scope?` | `"bypass" \| ((scope: Scope, query: unknown) => unknown)` | How the admin-wide `scope` narrows this resource. `"bypass"` opts out explicitly. |
| `access?` | `ResourceAccess<Row>` | Canonical operation-level authorization. |
| `fieldAccess?` | `FieldAccessMap<Row>` | Canonical read/write policy for declared fields. |
| `export?` | `{ formats?: ("csv" \| "json")[]; fields?: (keyof Row & string)[] } \| false` | Export button, off unless set. `formats` defaults to `["csv"]`; `fields` defaults to the visible columns. |
| `import?` | `{ formats?: ("csv" \| "json")[]; fields?: (keyof Row & string)[] } \| false` | Import button. Off unless set; rows are created through the normal write path. |
| `audit?` | `boolean` | Opt this resource out of the admin-wide audit sink. |
| `realtime?` | `boolean \| string` | Refresh the list when the channel fires. `true` uses `resource.<name>`. |
| `views?` | `Array<{ name: string; description?: string; /** Filter values keyed by the row's fields: a value, a preset name for a `daterange`, `{ gte, lte }` or an array. */ filters?: ListFilters<Row>; sort?: { field: keyof Row & string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }; search?: string; }>` | Filter / sort presets offered as a dropdown above the list. |
| `empty?` | `{ /** Serializable Lucide icon rendered above the empty-state title. */ icon?: IconName; title?: string; description?: string; action?: { label: string; href: string }; /** * Title when search or filters leave no rows; a button beside it clears them. `{query}` is * the search text. Default: `labels.widget.filtered`. */ filtered?: string; /** * Title when a search leaves no rows, in place of `filtered`, e.g. `"Nothing found for «{query}»"`. * Default: `filtered`. */ searched?: string; }` | What the list shows when there are no rows at all. |

An empty list shows `empty.title`, `description`, `icon` and `action`. When search
or filters leave no rows it shows `empty.filtered` (or `empty.searched` during a
search; both fill `{query}`) and a button that clears them. On a phone the list
shows 10 rows as cards with the rest behind "N more".

#### Detail headings and editing

Three callbacks fill the record page header. Each receives the row's readable
declared and `detail.expose` fields.

- `detail.title(row)` is the `h1` content: text or inline elements.
- `detail.subtitle(row)` is the line under it.
- `detail.badge(row)` is a pill beside the title: `{ label, tone }`.

```ts excerpt
detail: {
  title: (row) => row.email,
  subtitle: (row) => `Customer since ${row.createdAt}`,
  badge: (row) => (row.churned ? { label: "Churned", tone: "warn" } : null),
}
```

A nullish return leaves the slot empty; a nullish `title` falls back to the row's
`name`, `title` or `email`, then to the resource label and the row identifier.

The Edit button sits beside the heading as a secondary button;
`update: { emphasis: "primary" }` fills it. It is hidden when `update.disabled` is
set or the update policy denies the request. A custom `PageHeader` slot uses the
exported `PageHeaderProps`.

Without `detail.tabs`, the page renders one key/value block. `detail.fields`
chooses and orders the fields in it; omitted, every readable declared field shows.

#### Opening a row

`rowClick` decides what a click on a row, or Enter on it, does.

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `"detail"` | Navigates to the row's own page under `paths.admin`. |
| `"drawer"` | Opens the [drawer](/docs/reference/drawer). Requires a `drawer` config; `defineAdmin` refuses the combination without one. |
| `false` | Rows render, but a click does nothing. |

Omitted, it follows the resource: `"drawer"` when a drawer is configured, with or
without `detail`, and `"detail"` otherwise. The record page renders without a
`detail` config, so every row opens unless you set `rowClick: false`.
An explicit value always wins, so `rowClick: "detail"` on a resource that also
has a drawer sends the click to the page and leaves the drawer to its own
affordances.

A row without a key never opens. Opening is a router push, not a link, so
cmd-click does not open a new tab; add a column whose `render` returns an anchor
for that.

In a row that opens, an `editable` column starts editing from its pencil icon, a
double click or Enter; a single click opens the row.

#### Reading a view

A resource's ref may be a database view. The list, the record page, counts, exports,
reference labels, related tabs and `ctx.read` read the view; create, update, delete,
restore, import and inline edits write to `writeTo`:

```ts excerpt
resource(adminUserRow, {
  name: "user",
  writeTo: user,
  update: { fields: [{ name: "internal", type: "switch" }] },
});
```

`writeTo` must be a table whose primary key the view selects. Every field a form or an
inline `editable` column writes must be a column of both: form fields are typed against the view's row, so select each
writable column in the view. `defineAdmin` checks both and names the missing column. The
write schema is inferred from `writeTo`, the generated edit form offers the table's
writable columns, and an update answers with the view's row, so computed columns are fresh
after a save.

Without `writeTo`, a resource over a view is read-only: its create, update and delete are
disabled, and declaring any of them (or `import`, or an `editable` column) throws at
`defineAdmin`.

#### Icons

Resource, dashboard, page, queue, action and command icons take an `IconName`, a
Lucide icon name such as `users`, `settings`, `database` or `trash-2`. An unknown
name is a type error. To render one in your own component:

```tsx excerpt
import { FlowpanelIcon } from "@flowpanel/kit/react";

<FlowpanelIcon name="workflow" className="size-4" />;
```

#### Saved views

`views` puts named filter, sort and search presets in a menu above the list.
Filters are keyed by the row's fields:

```ts excerpt
views: [
  { name: "New this week", filters: { createdAt: "last7d" } },
  { name: "Paying, falling asleep", filters: { plan: ["starter", "pro"], daysSinceSeen: { gte: 7 } } },
  { name: "No Telegram", filters: { telegramLinked: false } },
],
```

A `daterange` filter also takes a preset name (`today`, `yesterday`, `last7d`,
`last30d`, `MTD`, `QTD`, `YTD`), resolved on each request. A view may filter only
fields the list declares in `columns`, `filters` or `search`, with values that
match the filter type; `defineAdmin` rejects the rest. For "older than N days",
compute the number in a view and use a `numeric-range` filter.

### ColumnDef

An entry in `columns`. A bare string is shorthand for `{ field: "name" }`.

`ColumnDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field?` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this column reads. Omit only when `render` supplies the cell. |
| `secondary?` | `keyof Row & string` | Another field of the row, shown as a muted second line under the cell — the email under a name. It is loaded with the row; sort and search still use `field`. Ignored on a `reference` column. |
| `label?` | `string` | Header text. Defaults to a humanized `field`. |
| `render?` | `(row: Row, ctx: RequestContext) => ReactNode` | Custom cell renderer. Runs on the server; receives the request context. |
| `sortable?` | `boolean` | Allow clicking the header to sort by this column. |
| `width?` | `number \| string` | Fixed column width, in px when a number. |
| `align?` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | Horizontal cell alignment. Defaults to `"left"`. |
| `className?` | `string` | Extra classes on every cell in this column. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Keep the column out of the table (still available to export and drawer). |
| `format?` | `ColumnFormat` | Declarative cell formatting — use instead of `render` where it fits. |
| `reference?` | `ReferenceSpec` | Resolve a foreign key to a label from another resource. |
| `editable?` | `boolean` | Allow editing this cell inline from the list. |

A column without `field` must set `render` and `label`; it never sorts or
filters and is skipped by export. See
[Joined or computed values](/docs/customization/column-renderers#joined-or-computed-values).

`secondary` shows another field as a muted second line in the cell, such as the
email under a name. Sorting and search still use `field`.

```ts excerpt
columns: [{ field: "name", label: "User", secondary: "email" }],
```

#### ColumnFormat

Declarative cell formatting.

```ts excerpt
type ColumnFormat =
  | "badge" | "money" | "number"
  | "date" | "relative" | "percent" | "duration" | "boolean" | "url"
  | { kind: "badge"; tones?: Record<string, Tone>; labels?: Record<string, string> }
  | { kind: "money"; currency?: string; scale?: number }
  | { kind: "number"; tones?: Threshold }
  | { kind: "date"; time?: boolean; calendarDay?: boolean }
  | { kind: "percent"; digits?: number; heat?: boolean; tones?: Threshold }
  | { kind: "duration"; unit?: "ms" | "s"; tones?: Threshold }
  | { kind: "boolean"; labels?: { true?: string; false?: string } }
  | { kind: "url"; label?: string };
```

`Tone` is `"default" | "accent" | "ok" | "warn" | "err" | "info" | "muted"`.
The object form of `badge` maps each cell value to a tone:

```ts excerpt
{ field: "status", format: { kind: "badge", tones: { paid: "ok", failed: "err" } } }
```

`labels` gives each raw value its display text. Tones stay keyed by the raw
value, and a value with no label shows as is.

```ts excerpt
{
  field: "role",
  format: {
    kind: "badge",
    tones: { admin: "warn" },
    labels: { admin: "Administrator", freelancer: "Freelancer" },
  },
}
```

The other kinds:

- `date` shows the day in the admin's `timeZone`; `{ kind: "date", time: true }` adds the time. A `YYYY-MM-DD` value shows as itself; a zoneless `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` is read as UTC. Set `calendarDay: true` for a SQL `date` column, such as a Prisma `@db.Date` or a Drizzle `date({ mode: "date" })`: the driver returns midnight UTC, and the cell shows that day in every time zone.
- `relative` shows how long ago, such as `5 minutes ago`, in the admin's `locale`.
- `percent` reads a fraction: `0.423` is `42.3%`. `digits` caps the decimals, and `heat: true` shades the cell by its value, for a retention grid that still sorts by number.
- `duration` reads milliseconds, or seconds with `unit: "s"`, and prints the largest units that fit: `4.2 sec`, `2 hr 5 min`.
- `boolean` prints `✓` and `✕`, or `labels: { true: "Yes", false: "No" }`. SQLite's `1` and `0` read as true and false.
- `url` links `http(s)` and same-site values. `label` replaces the text, which defaults to the host and path; any other scheme stays text.
- `{ kind: "number" | "percent" | "duration", tones }` colours the text by a [`Threshold`](/docs/reference/widgets#thresholds), comparing the stored number, so a `duration` in seconds compares seconds. With `tones`, a percent cell is coloured instead of shaded.

```ts excerpt
columns: [
  { field: "week", label: "Cohort" },
  { field: "w1", label: "Week 1", format: { kind: "percent", heat: true } },
  { field: "p95Ms", label: "p95", format: "duration" },
  { field: "url", format: "url" },
  { field: "lastSeenAt", label: "Last seen", format: "relative" },
]
```

`relative` renders a `<time>` with the exact timestamp in its tooltip, and `url`
opens absolute URLs in a new tab without opening the row.

#### Formatting values yourself

The formatters behind every cell, card and export. Each takes the admin's
resolved `formatting`.

`formatColumnValue` renders a `ColumnFormat`; `formatNumber` renders a widget's
`NumericFormat` (`number`, `currency`, `percent`, `bytes`, `duration`). Import both
from `@flowpanel/kit`; `@flowpanel/kit/react` also exports `formatNumber`.
`formatDurationValue`, `formatPercentValue` and `formatRelativeValue` print one
kind each.

### Enums

`enumOf()` declares an enum's labels and tones once, for a column's `format`,
filter and field `options`, badges and timeline chips.

```ts excerpt
import { enumOf, resource } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import { planEnum, users } from "@/db/schema";

export const Plan = enumOf(planEnum.enumValues, {
  free: ["Free", "muted"],
  starter: ["Starter", "info"],
  pro: { label: "Pro", tone: "accent" },
});

resource(users, {
  columns: [{ field: "plan", format: Plan.format }],
  filters: [{ field: "plan", type: "select", options: Plan.options }],
  detail: { badge: (user) => Plan.badge(user.plan) },
});
```

With the database enum's values first, a missing or extra label is a compile
error; otherwise the entry keys are the values. An entry is a label, a
`[label, tone]` pair or `{ label, tone }`. `label()` prints an unknown value as
itself and a missing one as `—`; `badge()` returns `null` for a missing value;
`badge(value, { href })` makes the pill a link.

`EnumDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | `readonly K[]` | Every value, in declaration order. |
| `labels` | `Readonly<Record<K, string>>` |  |
| `tones` | `Readonly<Record<K, Tone>>` |  |
| `format` | `{ kind: "badge"; labels: Readonly<Record<K, string>>; tones: Readonly<Record<K, Tone>>; }` | A badge column format with these labels and tones. Plain data: safe anywhere. |
| `options` | `SelectOption[]` | `{ label, value }` in declaration order, for a filter, a form field or a dashboard filter. |
| `label` | `(value: unknown) => string` | The label; an unknown value prints as itself, a missing one as `"—"`. |
| `tone` | `(value: unknown) => Tone` | The tone; `"default"` for an unknown value. |
| `badge` | `(value: unknown, options?: { href?: LinkTarget }) => { label: string; tone: Tone; href?: LinkTarget } \| null` | A header badge, or `null` for a nullish value; `href` links it, e.g. to the filtered list. |

### FieldDef

An entry in `create.fields`, `update.fields`, a `DetailTab`, or an action's
`form`. `required` marks the control required and the server rejects a missing
value. `readOnly` and `requireRole` apply to rendering and to writes; a function
`readOnly` is called with the stored row, so it guards edits. `hidden` only removes
the control.

`FieldDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this field writes. |
| `label?` | `string` | Field label. Defaults to a humanized `name`. |
| `help?` | `string` | Hint rendered under the control. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | Placeholder text for empty inputs. |
| `type?` | `FieldType` | Which control to render. Omitted, a declared field renders as `"text"` — or `"reference"` when `reference` is set. The adapter's column type is consulted only by a fully generated form, and only maps number, boolean, date and json. |
| `options?` | `\| ReadonlyArray<string> \| SelectOption[] \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<SelectOption[]>)` | Choices for `select` / `multiselect` / `radio`. A function resolves per request. |
| `reference?` | `ReferenceSpec` | Turn the field into a searchable picker over another resource. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | Require a value. The form marks it, and the server rejects a create that leaves it empty or an edit that clears it. |
| `readOnly?` | `boolean \| ((values: Partial<Row>) => boolean)` | Render non-editable. Enforced server-side, not just in the UI. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean \| ((values: Partial<Row>) => boolean)` | Leave the field out of the form entirely. |
| `requireRole?` | `string \| string[] \| ((session: Session \| null) => boolean)` | Restrict who may see and write this field. Enforced on every write route. |
| `validate?` | `\| z.ZodTypeAny \| ((value: unknown, values: Partial<Row>) => string \| null \| Promise<string \| null>)` | Per-field validation, run server-side after the resource schema. |
| `defaultValue?` | `unknown \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<unknown>)` | Value used when creating, for keys the operator left empty. |
| `span?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Width in a 12-column form grid. Defaults to full width. |
| `group?` | `string` | Fieldset heading this field is grouped under. |
| `render?` | `(row: Row, ctx: RequestContext) => ReactNode \| Promise<ReactNode>` | Detail pages and drawers only: what the field shows instead of its value — a join or a computed label. |

#### FieldType

```ts excerpt
type FieldType =
  | "text" | "textarea" | "number" | "email" | "password" | "url"
  | "date" | "datetime" | "time"
  | "boolean" | "switch" | "checkbox"
  | "select" | "multiselect" | "radio"
  | "json" | "markdown" | "tags" | "reference" | "hidden" | "color";
```

Without `type`, a field is `"text"`, or `"reference"` when it sets `reference`.
Only a fully generated form (no `create.fields` or `update.fields`) reads the
column type, and only for numbers, booleans, dates and JSON.

### FilterDef

An entry in `filters`. A bare string is a `text` filter; set `type` for anything
else. A `select` or `multiselect` filter without `options` on a column formatted
with badge `labels`, such as an `enumOf` format, lists those labels.

`FilterDef`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `keyof Row & string` | Row property this filter narrows. |
| `label?` | `string` | Control label. Defaults to a humanized `field`. |
| `type` | `FilterType` | Which control to render, and how the value is encoded in the URL. |
| `options?` | `\| ReadonlyArray<string> \| SelectOption[] \| ((ctx: QueryContext) => Promise<SelectOption[]>)` | Choices for `select` / `multiselect`. A function is resolved per request. |
| `defaultValue?` | `unknown` | Applied while the URL names no value for the filter: the list, its count, pages, export and API all read it. Clearing the control writes an empty `f_<field>=` so the default stays off; a view or link turns it off with `null`. |
| `hidden?` | `boolean` | Apply the filter, and its `defaultValue`, without showing a control for it. |

#### Default and hidden filters

`defaultValue` applies while the URL has no value for the filter, to the rows,
totals and export alike. Clearing it writes an empty `f_<field>=` to the URL. A
saved view or link turns it off with `null`. `hidden: true` applies the filter
without a control.

```ts excerpt
filters: [
  { field: "isTest", label: "Test accounts", type: "boolean", defaultValue: false },
],
views: [{ name: "Everyone", filters: { isTest: null } }],
```

A filter compares one column. To filter by an expression or through a relation,
read the resource from a view that computes the column and set
[`writeTo`](#reading-a-view).

#### FilterType

```ts excerpt
type FilterType =
  | "text" | "select" | "multiselect"
  | "daterange" | "numeric-range" | "boolean" | "tag";
```

`daterange` and `numeric-range` reach your adapter as a `FilterRangeValue`;
`multiselect` as a `FilterInValue`. Both are documented under
[Contexts](/docs/reference/contexts#filter-values).

### Record page

`detail` configures `<paths.admin>/<resource>/<id>`. Type a card that lives in its own file
with `DetailOptions<Row>`:

```ts excerpt
import { type DetailOptions, kv, metric, related, type RowOf } from "@flowpanel/kit";

export const card = {
  title: (u) => u.name ?? u.email,
  subtitle: (u, { format }) => `with us since ${format.date(u.createdAt)}`,
  badge: (u) => [Lifecycle.badge(u.lifecycle), Plan.badge(u.plan)],
  dateRange: { preset: "last30d", presets: ["last7d", "last30d", "QTD"] },
  stats: [metric("Visits", { count: "user_visit", range: "startedAt" }, { compare: true })],
  aside: [kv({ label: "Profile", columns: 1, items: [{ label: "Email", field: "email" }] })],
  tabs: [related("response")],
} satisfies DetailOptions<RowOf<"user">>;
```

- `title`, `subtitle` and `badge` receive the row and a `DetailHeaderContext`: the
  admin's `format`, `labels` and `link`. `badge` returns one pill or a list, in order;
  `null` entries are dropped, and a pill with `href` is a link.
- `stats` renders as a hairline strip under the header, on every tab.
- `aside` is a column beside the tabs from the `lg` breakpoint and below them on a phone,
  on every tab.
- `dateRange` adds a date picker to the header. Its range, with `previous`, reaches
  `stats`, `aside` and every widgets tab. Related rows list every row, a
  [timeline](/docs/reference/widgets#timeline) pages through the whole history and a
  heatmap shows its last `days` days. Without `dateRange` the page has no picker and
  widgets see the record's whole history.

The header, strip, aside and open tab share one widget context, so a repeated
`ctx.count`, `ctx.read` or `ctx.query` runs once per page.

`DetailOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expose?` | `(keyof Row & string)[]` | Extra fields used only by detail headers, hidden-tab predicates, related filters, or custom detail renderers. They never widen list rows. |
| `title?` | `(row: Row, ctx: DetailHeaderContext) => ReactNode \| string \| null \| undefined` | Heading content (inside h1). Receives declared, readable detail fields; nullish output uses `<label> · <pk>`. |
| `subtitle?` | `(row: Row, ctx: DetailHeaderContext) => MaybePromise<string \| null \| undefined>` | One line under the heading, for the fact that identifies the record. May be async. |
| `badge?` | `( row: Row, ctx: DetailHeaderContext, ) => MaybePromise<DetailBadge \| ReadonlyArray<DetailBadge \| null \| undefined> \| null \| undefined>` | Pills beside the heading: one, or several in order; nullish entries are dropped. May be async. |
| `dateRange?` | `DateRangeConfig` | A date picker in the header; its range, with `previous`, reaches `stats`, `aside` and every widgets tab. Omitted: the whole history, and no picker. |
| `stats?` | `Array<StatWidget \| MetricWidget>` | Numbers in a hairline strip under the header, on every tab. |
| `aside?` | `WidgetConfig[]` | Widgets in a column beside the tabs from the `lg` breakpoint, below them on a phone, on every tab. |
| `tabs?` | `DetailTab<Row>[]` |  |
| `fields?` | `(keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] \| "*"` |  |

#### DetailHeaderContext

`DetailHeaderContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `WidgetFormat` | The admin's formatters — locale, zone and currency from `formatting`. |
| `labels` | `ResolvedLabels` | The admin's resolved chrome strings. |
| `link` | `(target: LinkTarget) => string` | Resolves a link target to an href under the admin's mount. |

#### DetailBadge

`DetailBadge`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `tone?` | `Tone` |  |
| `href?` | `LinkTarget` | Makes the pill a link — a path or a named target. |

### DetailTab

A tab on the record page. The open tab is the `?tab=<key>` query parameter, and
only that tab runs on the server.

A tab shows `render` when it has one. Otherwise it shows its `widgets` and its
`resource` list, widgets above the rows, or its fields when it has neither.

#### Fields and sections

`fields` renders key/value pairs; `"*"` shows every readable field. An entry is a
field name or a `FieldDef`. Column `format` and `render` apply here too.

A `FieldDef` with `render(row, ctx)` shows its result instead of the value. It
runs on the server, only when the reader may read `name`, concurrently with the
tab's other renders. A render that throws is logged and the field shows its
formatted value; see [server-rendered cells](/docs/reference/drawer#server-rendered-cells)
for the drawer:

```ts excerpt
{
  name: "categoryId",
  label: "Category",
  render: async (job, ctx) => {
    const category = await findCategory(ctx, job.categoryId);
    return `${category.title} (${category.openJobs})`;
  },
}
```

`sections` groups those fields into titled blocks and wins over `fields` on the
same tab:

```ts excerpt
{
  key: "overview",
  label: "Overview",
  sections: [
    { label: "Identity", fields: ["email", "name"] },
    { label: "Billing", fields: [{ name: "mrr", label: "MRR" }, "plan"] },
  ],
}
```

Fields named here are loaded when the tab is open. A field the reader may not
read is left out.

#### Widgets

`widgets` puts dashboard widgets in the tab; see
[widget tabs](/docs/build/detail-cards#widget-tabs). `columns` defaults to 2, or 12
once a widget sets `span`. `ctx.row` is the record. A failing widget shows its own
error card.

#### Related rows

A tab with `resource` shows that resource's list columns, paged under the URL key
`relatedPage.<key>` and sorted under `relatedSort.<key>`. `hide` drops columns and
their values; the parent foreign key is the usual one. `sort` sets the default
order. An "Open list" link to the filtered list appears when every filter value is
a scalar on a field the target declares.

`filter` is a constraint: an undefined parent value yields no rows and no query.
A row opens by the target's [`rowClick`](#opening-a-row); a drawer opens over the
record page under `?drawer=<resource>:<id>`.

`pageSize` defaults to 25. `count: true` shows the row count in the label.
`widgets` on the same tab render above the rows.

`by` names the target's field that points at this record: it becomes `filter`, reading the
record's `rowKey`, and `hide`, unless you give those yourself.

#### Related tabs in one line

`related(resource, options)` builds a counted related tab. Without `by`, `defineAdmin` finds
the one column of the target whose `reference.resource` is this resource and uses it; none
or several throw and ask for `by`. `by`, `hide` and `sort.field` are fields of the target's
row, so a typo is a compile error once resources are typed, and `defineAdmin` names the
closest column otherwise. The label defaults to the target's `plural`.

```ts excerpt
detail: {
  tabs: [
    related("response", { label: "Responses", widgets: [responseFunnel] }),
    related("payment", { pageSize: 10, sort: { field: "createdAt", dir: "desc" } }),
  ],
}
```

A tab with neither `by` nor `filter` reads every row of its target.

`RelatedOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key?` | `string` | The tab's URL key. Default: `the resource name`. |
| `label?` | `string` | Tab label. Default: `the target's `plural`, else its `label`, else its humanised name`. |
| `by?` | `Field<N>` | The target's field that points at the record. Omitted: inferred from its `reference`. |
| `count?` | `boolean` | Show the row count in the label. Default: `true`. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Rows per page. Default: `25`. |
| `sort?` | `{ field: Field<N>; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }` | Default order of the rows. |
| `hide?` | `Field<N>[]` | Columns to leave out. Default: ``[by]``. |
| `widgets?` | `WidgetConfig[]` | Widgets above the rows, with `ctx.row` set to the record being viewed. |
| `columns?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Grid columns for `widgets`. |
| `emptyState?` | `string` | Shown instead of the generic label when there are no rows. |
| `hidden?` | `(row: Record<string, unknown>) => boolean` | Hide the tab for records that should not show it. |

#### Empty state

`emptyState` replaces the default text when a tab has no rows, widgets or
readable fields.

```ts excerpt
{ key: "runs", label: "Runs", resource: "runs", filter: (u) => ({ userId: u.id }), emptyState: "No runs yet" }
```

#### Custom content

`render(row, ctx)` returns any React content. `row` holds the declared and
`detail.expose` fields; `ctx` is a [`DetailTabContext`](#detailtabcontext).

`DetailTab`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, stored in the URL's `?tab=` search parameter. |
| `label` | `string` | Tab label. |
| `hidden?` | `(row: Row) => boolean` | Hide the tab for rows that should not show it. |
| `fields?` | `(keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] \| "*"` | Field list to render as a key/value view. `"*"` shows every column. |
| `sections?` | `Array<{ label: string; fields: (keyof Row \| FieldDef<Row>)[] }>` | Grouped key/value fields, one block per entry. Wins over `fields`. |
| `resource?` | `ResourceName` | Render rows of a related resource instead of fields. |
| `filter?` | `(row: Row) => Record<string, unknown>` | Filter applied to `resource`, derived from the row being viewed. |
| `by?` | `string` | The target's field that points at this record; becomes `filter` and `hide` unless those are given. A `related()` tab infers it from the one target column whose `reference.resource` is this resource. |
| `count?` | `boolean` | Show the row count in the tab's label — `"Responses · 12"`. Default: `false; true through `related()``. |
| `pageSize?` | `number` | Related rows per page. Default: `25`. |
| `hide?` | `string[]` | Related-tab columns to omit, typically the parent foreign key. |
| `sort?` | `{ field: string; dir: "asc" \| "desc" }` | Related-tab default sort; falls back to the target's `defaultSort`, then its primary key. |
| `widgets?` | `WidgetConfig[]` | Dashboard widgets with `ctx.row` set to the record being viewed; with `resource`, above its rows. |
| `columns?` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 6 \| 12` | Grid columns for `widgets`; omitted, 12 when a widget sets `span`. Default: `2`. |
| `render?` | `(row: Row, ctx: DetailTabContext) => ReactNode` | Render arbitrary content instead of fields, widgets or a related resource. |
| `emptyState?` | `string` | Shown instead of the generic label when the tab has nothing to show: no related rows, no widgets, or no fields the reader may see. |

### DetailTabContext

What `DetailTab.render` receives as its second argument.

`DetailTabContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `DB` | Your database client, exactly as handed to the adapter. |
| `session` | `Session \| null` |  |
| `dateRange` | `WidgetDateRange` | The picked range, the period before it and the admin's zone, resolved to dates. |
| `labels` | `ResolvedLabels` | The admin's resolved chrome strings, so a widget never hard-codes English. |
| `query` | `{ <T>(key: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; <A extends unknown[], T>(fn: (...args: A) => Promise<T>, ...args: A): Promise<T>; <T>(fn: (ctx: WidgetContext<DB>) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>; }` | Memoises a query per request: a key and a thunk, or a function and its arguments. A function passed alone that declares a parameter is called with this context: `query(hourly)` runs `hourly(ctx)`. |
| `sql` | `<Row = Record<string, unknown>>( strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[] ) => Promise<Row[]>` | One read-only statement, as a tagged template; every interpolated value binds as a parameter, never as text. Runs exactly the statement you write — no tenant scope, access rule or soft-delete filter applied; `count`/reads do. |
| `count` | `<N extends ResourceName>( resource: N, where?: Where<RowOf<N>>, options?: CountOptions<RowOf<N>>, ) => Promise<number>` | How many rows of a registered resource match `where`, under the same role, access and scope checks as its list. Memoised per request by resource, `where` and range; a resource the session may not read counts `0`. |
| `read` | `<N extends ResourceName>( resource: N, options?: ReadOptions<RowOf<N>>, ) => Promise<RowOf<N>[]>` | Rows of a registered resource under the same role, access, scope, field and soft-delete rules as its list. Memoised per request by resource and options; a resource the session may not read returns `[]`. |
| `rowOf` | `<N extends ResourceName>(resource: N) => RowOf<N>` | The record this card shows, typed by its resource. Throws on a dashboard, which has no record, and on another resource's card; the message names both. |
| `id?` | `string` | The viewed record's key as a string — `row[rowKey]`. Absent on a dashboard, or when the key is not a string or number. |
| `format` | `WidgetFormat` | The admin's formatters — locale, zone and currency from `formatting`. |
| `link` | `(target: LinkTarget) => string` | Resolve a link target to an href, for the props of a custom widget. |

### SelectOption

```ts excerpt
type SelectOption = { label: string; value: string | number | boolean };
```

A filter's or field's `options` takes `string[]`, `SelectOption[]`, or a function
resolved per request. A dashboard filter takes `SelectOption[]`, an `enumOf()`, or
a function of the widget context. A drawer action input takes `string[]`.

### ListResult

What a `list` returns, from the adapter through to the pagination control.

`ListResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `Row[]` |  |
| `total` | `number` | Total matching rows across every page — drives the pagination control. |
| `page` | `number` | 1-based index of the page in `rows`. |
| `pageSize` | `number` |  |

### ResourceConfig

What `resource()` returns.

`ResourceConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__kind` | `"resource"` |  |
| `ref` | `Ref` |  |
| `options` | `ResourceOptions<Row> & Options` |  |

## Actions

Every option of row, bulk, dashboard and drawer actions, and what they return.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/actions

Documented types: rowAction, RowAction, bulkAction, BulkAction, dashboardAction, DashboardAction, DrawerAction, DrawerFieldFormSpec, ActionResult, ActionContext

Row, bulk, dashboard and drawer actions share one result type and one guard
order: the admin role gate, the resource gate, then the action's own
`access`, all before `run`. Each is a POST route under `/api/flowpanel/…`.
Guide: [Add actions](/docs/build/actions).

### RowAction

Offered on a single row, inline or in the row menu. `rowAction<Row, Input>()` types
both `run` arguments and checks every `form[].name` against `Input`; it returns the
object unchanged. Add it to a resource's `actions`.

```ts twoslash
import { rowAction } from "@flowpanel/kit";

type User = { id: string; status: "active" | "suspended" };
type SuspendInput = { reason: string; notify: boolean };

export const suspendUser = rowAction<User, SuspendInput>({
  key: "suspend",
  label: "Suspend",
  icon: "ban",
  form: [
    { name: "reason", type: "textarea", required: true },
    { name: "notify", type: "checkbox" },
  ],
  run: async (user, input) => ({
    ok: true,
    message: `${user.id}: ${input.reason}`,
  }),
});
```

`RowAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `placement?` | `"inline" \| "menu"` | `"inline"` renders a button in the row; `"menu"` puts it in the row menu. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `hidden?` | `(row: Row, ctx: RequestContext) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Hide the action for rows it does not apply to. Evaluated server-side per row. |
| `disabled?` | `(row: Row) => boolean \| string` | Disable with a reason. A string is shown to the operator. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Server-enforced row condition, evaluated only after a scoped row load. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(row: Row, input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

`hidden` runs on the server per row; a hidden action's route returns `404` for
that row.

### BulkAction

Runs on the selection. `run` receives the IDs. `max` caps the selection, 1000 by
default and at most 10000; over it the route answers `422 too many ids (max N)` and
`run` does not execute.

`BulkAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `max?` | `number` | Maximum selected ids accepted by this action, from 1 to 10000. Default: `1000`. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(ids: string[], input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler, given every selected id, never more than `max`. |

`bulkAction<Row, Input>()` types the form input. With delete enabled and no
`bulkActions`, a default bulk delete is added; `bulkActions: []` removes it.

### DashboardAction

Rendered in the dashboard header. It gets only the form input.

`DashboardAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `icon?` | `IconName` | Serializable Lucide icon rendered beside the label. |
| `variant?` | `ActionVariant` | Button styling. |
| `emphasis?` | `ActionEmphasis` | `"primary"` fills the button with the accent; keep one per dashboard, as more warn in development. Default: `"secondary"`. |
| `confirm?` | `ActionConfirm` | Ask for confirmation before running. |
| `form?` | `FieldDef<Input>[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `input`. |
| `inputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Input>` | Cross-field input validation for trusted action code. |
| `outputSchema?` | `z.ZodType<Output>` | Required before arbitrary `data` may cross the client boundary. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Restrict the action to a role. Enforced before `run`. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `(input: Input, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>) => Promise<ActionResult<Output>>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

Actions are secondary buttons, destructive ones in the error colour.
`emphasis: "primary"` fills one with the accent; more than one primary on a
dashboard warns in development.

```ts excerpt
dashboardAction({ key: "retry", label: "Retry failed runs", emphasis: "primary", run: retryFailed });
```

`hideActionsBar: true` on the dashboard hides the bar.

### DrawerAction

Rendered in the drawer footer. Its `form` uses `DrawerFieldFormSpec`.

`DrawerAction`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier, used in the action's URL. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `variant?` | `"default" \| "destructive"` | `"destructive"` styles the button as dangerous. |
| `confirm?` | `string` | Ask for confirmation with this message before running. |
| `form?` | `DrawerFieldFormSpec[]` | Inputs collected before `run`, passed to it as `formData`. |
| `palette?` | `boolean` | Also offer the action in the command palette. |
| `access?` | `AccessRule` | Roles allowed to see and execute this action. |
| `when?` | `(context: FieldWriteContext<Row>) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Server-enforced row condition evaluated after the scoped row load. |
| `unsafe?` | `readonly "db"[]` | Explicitly opt trusted code into raw database access. |
| `run` | `( row: Row, formData: Record<string, unknown>, ctx: ActionContext<InferDB>, ) => Promise<ActionResult>` | Server-side handler. Runs only after every guard has passed. |

#### DrawerFieldFormSpec

`DrawerFieldFormSpec`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Key this input contributes to the action's `formData`. |
| `type?` | `"text" \| "textarea" \| "select" \| "switch" \| "number"` | Control to render. Defaults to `"text"`. |
| `options?` | `string[]` | Choices for `select`. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | Reject an empty value. Enforced server-side. |
| `validate?` | `\| z.ZodTypeAny \| ((value: unknown, values: Record<string, unknown>) => string \| null \| Promise<string \| null>)` | Per-input validation, run server-side before `run`. |

### ActionResult

What every `run` returns.

`ActionResult`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true` |  |
| `message?` | `string` | Toast shown to the operator. |
| `refresh?` | `boolean \| string \| string[]` | Revalidate after the action. `true` refreshes the current resource; a string publishes that one channel. |
| `redirect?` | `string` | Send the operator to this path once the action succeeds. |
| `download?` | `{ filename: string; data: string \| Blob \| Uint8Array; mime?: string }` | Hand the operator a generated file. |
| `filename` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `string \| Blob \| Uint8Array` |  |
| `mime?` | `string` |  |
| `data?` | `never` |  |
| `data?` | `Data` |  |
| `ok` | `false` |  |
| `error` | `string` | Message shown to the operator. Safe to display — never include internals. |
| `fieldErrors?` | `Record<string, string>` | Per-field messages, keyed by `FieldDef.name`, for actions with a `form`. |

`ActionInput` defaults to `Record<string, unknown>`. `{ ok: false, error }` shows
`error` to the operator as written. A thrown `FlowpanelError` keeps its status;
anything else becomes a `500` and goes to `hooks.onError`, or, without a hook, to one
`console.error` line with its request id.

### ActionContext

The last argument to every `run`.

`ActionContext`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unsafe?` | `{ db: Db }` | Explicit escape hatch for trusted action implementations. |
| `actorId` | `string \| null` | Caller identity — same derivation the audit trail uses (`auth.userId`, then `session.id`, then `session.user.id`). |
| `publish` | `(channel: string, payload?: unknown) => Promise<void>` | Push a realtime message to every connected admin. |

`ctx.unsafe.db` is the adapter's client, present only when the action declares `unsafe: ["db"]`. `ctx.publish` sends a realtime event.

### Validation

A `form` is validated on the server before `run`: `required`, then each field's
`validate`. A failure returns `422` with an `issues` array.

## Drawer

Layout, tabs and actions of the row side panel.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/drawer

Documented types: DrawerConfig, DrawerTabFields, DrawerTabResource, DrawerTabWidgets, DrawerAction, DrawerPayload

A drawer shows one row over the list. Declare `drawer` on a resource; a row click
opens it unless `rowClick` says otherwise. Guide: [Record pages and drawers](/docs/build/detail-cards#drawer).

```ts excerpt
resource(orders, {
  columns: ["id", "customerEmail", "status"],
  rowClick: "drawer",
  drawer: {
    width: "xl",
    title: (row) => `Order ${row.id}`,
    tabs: [
      { key: "summary", label: "Summary", fields: "*" },
      { key: "items", label: "Items", resource: "order_items", filter: (row) => ({ orderId: row.id }) },
    ],
    actions: [
      {
        key: "refund",
        label: "Refund",
        variant: "destructive",
        access: "admin",
        confirm: "Refund this order?",
        form: [{ name: "reason", type: "textarea", required: true }],
        run: async (row, formData, ctx) => {
          await refund(db, row.id, formData.reason as string);
          return { ok: true, message: "Refunded", refresh: true };
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

### DrawerConfig

`DrawerConfig`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width?` | `DrawerWidth` | Panel width. Default: `"lg"`. |
| `title?` | `(row: Row) => string` | Panel title. Defaults to the row's key. |
| `subtitle?` | `(row: Row) => string` | The line under the title. Defaults to the resource's label. |
| `fields?` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields shown when no `tabs` are declared. `"*"` shows every column. |
| `tabs?` | `DrawerTab<Row>[]` | Tabs to render instead of a flat field list. |
| `actions?` | `DrawerAction<Row>[]` | Buttons rendered in the panel footer. |

`DrawerWidth` is `"sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "full"`, defaulting to
`"lg"`.

With a `detail` page, the header links to it (`labels.drawer.viewDetails`). The
line under the title is the resource label unless you set `subtitle(row)`.

Without `tabs`, the drawer lists `fields` (`(keyof Row | FieldDef<Row>)[] | "*"`),
labelled and rendered by the matching columns. A `FieldDef.render` wins over the
column's; see [fields and sections](/docs/reference/resources#fields-and-sections).

#### Server-rendered cells

Renders in a drawer run concurrently on the server and become static HTML, so
return text or plain elements and use a pooled database client. A render that
returns a client component shows the list's cell or the formatted value instead.
A render that throws is logged as `[flowpanel] drawer render failed for "<field>"`
and the cell shows the formatted value.

### Tabs

`DrawerTab` is a union of three shapes, discriminated by which key you set.

#### DrawerTabFields

The row's own fields.

`DrawerTabFields`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | Stable identifier for the tab. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `fields` | `DrawerFieldList<Row>` | Fields to show. `"*"` shows every declared column. |

#### DrawerTabResource

Rows of a related resource, filtered by the open row.

`DrawerTabResource`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `resource` | `ResourceName` | Related resource to list. Must be registered on the same admin. |
| `filter?` | `(row: Row) => Record<string, unknown>` | Filter applied to the related resource, derived from the open row. |

The related resource's access rules apply; a tab the operator may not read is
empty. The tab shows the first 20 rows, with no pagination.

#### DrawerTabWidgets

Dashboard widgets, scoped to the open row.

`DrawerTabWidgets`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `widgets` | `Exclude< WidgetConfig, CustomWidget \| TimelineWidget \| HeatmapWidget \| ChecklistWidget \| TrackerWidget >[]` | `custom()`, `tracker()` and page-rendered widgets (`timeline`, `heatmap`, `checklist`) are not renderable here — the drawer serializes over the wire. |

`custom`, `timeline`, `heatmap`, `checklist` and `tracker` widgets are a type error
here, and the last four also fail at `defineAdmin`; use a record page tab. Each widget is serialized
before it reaches the browser:

```ts excerpt
type SerializedWidget =
  | { kind: "metric"; label: string; value: number | string; /* format, sublabel, tone, span, realtime */ }
  | { kind: "table"; rows: Record<string, unknown>[]; columns: { field: string; label?: string }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "statGroup"; stats: { label: string; value: string | number | CardDate; /* … */ }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "chart"; subkind: "area" | "bar" | "line" | "pie"; label: string; dataPoints: number; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "stat"; label: string; value: number | string | CardDate; /* format, hint, href, tone */ }
  | { kind: "kv"; items: { label: string; value: string | CardDate; /* tone, href, long, rest, more */ }[]; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "bars"; rows: { label: string; value: number; href?: string /* … */ }[]; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "funnel"; steps: { label: string; value: number; href?: string }[]; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "list"; rows: ListCardRow[]; more?: { label: string; href?: string }; emptyState: string; /* … */ }
  | { kind: "unsupported"; label?: string; reason: string; failed?: true; span?: number };
```

`CardDate` is `{ kind: "date"; iso: string }`, an instant the card renders in the
