  with a starting file for each and the `--db` and `--schema` flags that point at
  yours.
- **No terminal and no `--yes`, `--dry-run` or `--json`**: exits `1`. Pass `--yes`
  in CI.
- **A failed install**: keeps the files, prints the commands to run by hand, and
  exits `1`. So does an installed `@flowpanel/kit` or `@flowpanel/cli` from another
  minor version.

Re-running `init` keeps `flowpanel.config.ts` and skips matching files, and says
`Already set up; nothing changed.` when there is nothing to write. A conflicting
file stops it with nothing written and every conflicting path listed. `--yes`
accepts detected paths; it never overwrites.

### flowpanel migrate

`flowpanel migrate [options]` — Apply SQL migrations from flowpanel/migrations/
- `--dry-run` Print migrations that would be applied without running them
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Applies the SQL files in `flowpanel/migrations/` through your config's adapter,
loading the config with `jiti`.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel migrate
```

`--dry-run` lists the files without loading the config or connecting, so it cannot
tell which are applied. `--json` returns the pending and applied lists. Applied IDs
live in `_flowpanel_migrations`.

Without `flowpanel.config.ts` it exits `1` and says to run `init`, as `new` does.
Before it connects, it checks the connection variable your database client reads
(usually `DATABASE_URL`): when it is unset or empty, `migrate` exits `1` and says
what to set, so the driver never falls back to `localhost`. It reads the modules
the config imports `db` or `prisma` from, plus the Prisma schema; a variable with a
fallback in code, such as `?? "file:local.db"`, is not required. When the database
cannot be reached, the first line is `Cannot reach the database at
<host>:<port> (<code>). Check DATABASE_URL.` for Drizzle and Prisma alike;
the code is the socket error or Prisma's `P1001`, `P1002` or `P1017`.
`FLOWPANEL_DEBUG=1` adds the failed SQL and the stack trace. Under `--json` the
failure is a JSON document with an `error` field, and `applied` is `false` when
nothing ran.

Migrators are serialized at the database, and a concurrent duplicate is a no-op.
On PostgreSQL and SQLite each file and its marker share one transaction. MySQL
commits DDL implicitly: Drizzle holds an advisory lock and Prisma a claim row that
records where a failed run stopped. See [adapter migrations](/docs/reference/adapters#adapter).
Procedural scripts such as trigger bodies are rejected; run them with your ORM's
own migrations.

Every command reads `.env.local`, then `.env`; shell variables win.

### flowpanel doctor

`flowpanel doctor [options]` — Check FlowPanel health and wiring
- `--fix` Auto-fix missing route files from templates
- `--dry-run` Show fixes without writing (use with --fix)
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON
- `--path <path>` Resolved admin path when the config uses a dynamic one

Runs these checks:

- Next.js 15.5 or newer within 15 or 16, and TypeScript installed
- React and React DOM installed at supported, matching versions, and a supported Node.js
- an ORM the adapters support: Drizzle or Prisma
- `flowpanel.config.ts` exists; before `init`, this is the only check after the
  prerequisites, and its hint is `pnpm dlx @flowpanel/cli init`
- `@flowpanel/kit` is installed and matches the CLI's minor version
- the admin mount in the config (`paths.admin`) resolves to a static path
- the generated files exist: the API route, the SSE route, the seed migration and
  the catch-all admin page. A missing not-found page is a warning that `--fix` still
  repairs
- only one reachable `@flowpanel/core` installation across the installed
  dependency graph, including package-local peers and third-party plugins.
  Stale pnpm store entries are ignored; uninstalled projects skip this check
- no destructive row/bulk action declared without a `confirm`
- every ejected admin page still carries its eject marker
- with `cacheComponents` on: Next.js 16.3 or newer, no `runtime`, `dynamic`,
  `revalidate` or `fetchCache` export in the generated routes and admin page, and
  `instant = false` in the catch-all admin page and in an admin layout that reads the
  request. `--fix` adds it to a catch-all page `init` wrote; a page you edited gets
  the hint only
- `tsc --noEmit` passes. When `.next/types` is missing, `doctor` runs `next typegen`
  first, so the route and layout types Next generates exist
- `flowpanel.config.ts` evaluates; an error there is a failure with the error as
  its hint

Three more checks warn without failing the run: a session module that is still the
closed stub (`getSession` returns `null`) or the open development identity from
`init --dev-auth`, an empty `resources` array, and a missing `DATABASE_URL` while
`flowpanel/migrations/` holds SQL files. A warning prints as a yellow `!` line and
carries `"warn": true` in `--json`, where `hint` appears on failing and warning
checks only.

Mount checks follow route groups, parallel slots and intercepting routes.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor --fix
$ pnpm flowpanel doctor --fix --dry-run
```

`--fix` recreates missing generated files from the `init` templates, checks the files
again, then generates types and runs `tsc` once, so one run ends green when the files
were all that was missing. Other failures print a hint. A failed check exits non-zero, so it can run in CI.

### flowpanel eject

`flowpanel eject [options] <target> [name]` — Copy resource <name>, dashboard <path> or layout into your admin folder as code you own
- `<target>`
- `[name]`
- `--force` Overwrite files if they already exist
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Ejects a `resource`, `dashboard` or `layout` into your repo. See
[Eject to source](/docs/customization/eject).

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel eject resource users
$ pnpm flowpanel eject dashboard "/monitoring"
$ pnpm flowpanel eject layout
```

It writes the files under the admin mount, as one transaction. An ejected resource
stays in the config, because the ejected `actions.ts` reads rows through it; an ejected
dashboard's entry is commented out. When a target file exists, the plan is printed with
`Use --force to overwrite.`: a dry run exits `0` and a real run exits `1`. `--force`
replaces existing files. It follows a re-exporting root config and a `new --dir`
resources directory.

### flowpanel dev

`flowpanel dev [options]` — Run next dev, plus the queue board when REDIS_URL is set
- `--port <port>` Next.js dev port (default: 3000)
- `--no-board` Skip the queue board (bull-board) even if REDIS_URL is set

Runs `next dev`, plus the queue board (bull-board) when `scripts/board-server.mts`
(or `.ts`) exists and `REDIS_URL` is set. It runs the `next` binary installed in the
project with Node and never downloads one. A Yarn PnP project gets the message that
says how to set `nodeLinker` to `node-modules`. A busy port stops it with `Port <n> is in use. Pass --port
<other>.`

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel dev --port 3000
```

A port counts as busy when anything answers on `127.0.0.1` or `::1`.
Output is prefixed `[next]` and `[board]`; when Next.js is ready, `dev` prints the
admin URL. When one process exits, both stop.
`--no-board` skips the queue board. The board runs with `tsx` from your project, so
install it as a dev dependency (`pnpm add -D tsx`) when you use queues.

### flowpanel new

`flowpanel new [options] <resource>` — Add a resource for a table or model to the admin config
- `<resource>`
- `--table <expr>` The resource's first argument, as code (default: schema.<resource> on Drizzle, the model name on Prisma)
- `--kind <kind>` Adapter kind: drizzle or prisma (default: the config's adapter)
- `--dir <dir>` Write the resource to <dir>/<name>.ts and add it to <dir>/index.ts
- `--hidden` Register the resource without a navigation entry
- `--dry-run` Print the filesystem plan without writing
- `--json` Emit machine-readable JSON

Adds a resource to the config, or as its own file with `--dir`.

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel new posts
```

```text
└  Added resource "posts" to flowpanel.config.ts
```

It reads the table from your schema and adds an entry with its columns, search
fields, filters and default sort to the `resources` array, chosen the same way as
`--dir` below; an enum column gets a `select` filter. It also adds `resource` to the
`@flowpanel/kit` import when missing and removes the placeholder comment that `init`
wrote above the array. It checks the schema has the table, by SQL name or export
name, and exits `1` if not, or if the resource exists. It follows a root config that
re-exports another module, and when the config reads a `--dir` directory, `new`
writes there. `--hidden` without `--dir` adds `hidden: true` to the entry.

On Prisma it reads `schema.prisma`: `new users` resolves to the model mapped to
that table (`User`), and an unknown name exits `1` with the list of models. The
entry gets `name` set to the `@@map` table name, or the model in plural snake case
(`OrderItem` becomes `order_items`), so the URL and navigation read like a Drizzle
table's. A relation field becomes a `reference` when the target model already has a
resource. The model is added to `FlowpanelResources` under that name, so its rows and
the references to it are typed.

#### One file per resource

```bash
$ pnpm flowpanel new user_visit --dir admin/config/resources --hidden
```

`--dir` reads the Drizzle schema and writes `admin/config/resources/user-visit.ts`:

```ts excerpt
import { enumOf, resource } from "@flowpanel/kit";
import * as schema from "@/db/schema";

const Surface = enumOf(schema.activitySurface.enumValues, { web: "web", tma: "tma" });

export const userVisit = resource(schema.userVisit, {
  hidden: true,
  columns: [
    "id",
    { field: "userId", reference: { resource: "user", labelField: "name" } },
    { field: "surface", format: Surface.format },
    { field: "startedAt", format: { kind: "date", time: true } },
    "touches",
  ],
  filters: [{ field: "surface", type: "select" }],
  defaultSort: { field: "startedAt", dir: "desc" },
});
```

and adds it to `admin/config/resources/index.ts`. The first time, it also imports
that directory's `resources` into `flowpanel.config.ts` and spreads it into the
array; when the config is shaped differently it prints the line to add. Columns are chosen by type; an
enum gets an `enumOf` stub; a foreign key becomes a `reference` labelled by the
target's `name`, `title` or `email` when the target already has a file, so scaffold
referenced tables first. JSON and long text are left out, `name`, `title` and
`email` become search fields, and the list sorts by `createdAt` or `startedAt`.
`--hidden` keeps the resource out of the navigation.

Re-running changes nothing; a different existing file stops it. `--dir` is
Drizzle only. Without `--dir`, a config whose `resources` comes from a `--dir`
directory gets the new file there; any other `resources` that is not an array
literal is left unchanged, and `new` exits `1`.

`--table <expr>` sets the table expression, skips the schema check and writes empty
options. `--kind` defaults to the adapter the config builds.

## Testing

Walk every admin page in one Playwright call, and unit-test widgets and record headers over rows you pass.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/testing

Documented types: smokeAdmin, SmokeAdminOptions, SmokeAdminReport, A11yViolation, widgetContext, WidgetContextOptions, headerContext

`@flowpanel/test` is a dev dependency. `smokeAdmin` walks a running admin in
Playwright and fails on a broken page; `@flowpanel/test/widgets` unit-tests a
widget over rows you pass.

```sh
pnpm add -D @flowpanel/test @playwright/test
```

Install `@axe-core/playwright` too for the accessibility checks.

### smokeAdmin

```ts excerpt
import { test } from "@playwright/test";
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/test";

test("the admin is healthy", async ({ page }) => {
  await smokeAdmin(page, { paths: { admin: "/admin" }, a11y: true });
});
```

The walk starts at `paths.admin`, opens every dashboard and list in the navigation,
then opens each list's first row as its record page or drawer. On a record page it
opens every other tab as `?tab=<key>` (`tabs: false` skips them), so a failure
names its URL, such as `/admin/users/1?tab=activity`. A drawer is checked on its first tab.

### What it asserts

| Assertion | How it fails |
| --- | --- |
| Every navigation answers below 400 | `<route>: responded 500` |
| Nothing wrote to `console.error` | `console.error: <text>` |
| No page rendered `[data-fp-error]` | `<route>: rendered a FlowPanel error surface` |
| Zero WCAG 2.2 AA violations, with `a11y` | `<route>: axe <rule> (<impact>)` |
| The navigation has at least one route | `smokeAdmin found no navigation under <paths.admin> …` |

`[data-fp-error]` marks FlowPanel's error cards: a failed widget, a failed read, a
failed drawer. A walk that finds no routes fails. Pages count as loaded when `main`
is visible, since realtime pages never reach network idle.

### Options and report

`SmokeAdminOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paths?` | `{ admin?: string }` | Where the admin is mounted: the config's `paths.admin`. Default: `"/admin"`. |
| `cookie?` | `{ name: string; value: string; domain?: string }` | Session cookie added before the walk, for an admin behind authentication. |
| `resources?` | `string[]` | Restrict the walk to these nav segments — `"customers"` for `/admin/customers`. Every entry visited when omitted. |
| `a11y?` | `boolean` | Run axe against every visited route; needs `@axe-core/playwright`, or the walk skips the scan instead of failing. Default: `false`. |
| `maxRows?` | `number` | How many rows of each list the walk opens. Default: `1`. |
| `tabs?` | `boolean` | On each record page, open every other detail tab as `?tab=<key>` and check it the same way. Default: `true`. |

`SmokeAdminReport`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `visited` | `string[]` | Every route the walk loaded, in order, including rows it opened. |
| `consoleErrors` | `string[]` |  |
| `a11yViolations` | `A11yViolation[]` |  |

`A11yViolation`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `route` | `string` |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `impact?` | `string` |  |

`smokeAdmin` resolves with the report, or throws an `Error` listing each problem
and the report as JSON.

```ts excerpt
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/test";

const report = await smokeAdmin(page, {
  paths: { admin: "/admin" },
  cookie: { name: "session", value: process.env.E2E_SESSION ?? "" },
  resources: ["/", "customers", "orders"],
  maxRows: 3,
  a11y: true,
});

console.log(`${report.visited.length} routes visited`);
```

`resources` takes nav segments: `"/"` is the landing dashboard, `"customers"` is
`/admin/customers`. `cookie` is set on the admin's origin unless it has a `domain`.

### Unit-test a widget

`widgetContext` builds a widget context over rows you pass instead of a database.
`resolveWidget` runs the widget as a dashboard does and returns its card's props.

```ts excerpt
import { resolveWidget, widgetContext } from "@flowpanel/test/widgets";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { paidToday } from "@/admin/config/dashboards/money";

it("counts only today's paid invoices", async () => {
  const ctx = widgetContext({
    rows: {
      invoices: [
        { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date("2026-09-25T09:00:00Z") },
        { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date("2026-09-24T09:00:00Z") },
      ],
    },
    range: { from: new Date("2026-09-25T00:00:00Z"), to: new Date("2026-09-25T23:59:59Z") },
  });
  const { props } = await resolveWidget(paidToday, ctx);
  expect(props.value).toBe(1);
  expect(props.drilldown).toContain("/admin/invoices?f_status=paid");
});
```

`ctx.count`, `ctx.read`, `compare` and `ctx.link` run as in the admin. Without
`admin`, each key of `rows` is a resource whose columns are its rows' keys. Pass
`admin`, your `defineAdmin` config, when the widget needs views, dashboards or
references. Access rules apply, so pass `session` and `role`; tenant scope does not.

`sql` answers `ctx.sql`: rows, or a function of the statement and values. `row` and
`resource` make a record-page context. `filters` sets `ctx.filters`.

`WidgetContextOptions`

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows?` | `Readonly<Record<string, readonly Row[]>>` | Rows per resource name. `ctx.count`, `ctx.read`, `compare` and count metrics read them. |
| `admin?` | `ResolvedAdminConfig` | Your `defineAdmin` config, with only its database replaced by `rows`; carries no tenant scope. Without `admin`, every key of `rows` is a resource whose columns are the keys its rows carry. |
| `row?` | `Row` | The viewed record, for a record-page widget: `ctx.row`, `ctx.id` and `ctx.rowOf`. |
| `resource?` | `string` | The resource `row` belongs to; `ctx.rowOf` of another name throws. |
| `range?` | `{ from: Date; to: Date }` | The picked period; `compare` reads the one before it. Default: `the whole history until now`. |
| `filters?` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | The dashboard filters widgets read as `ctx.filters`. Default: `{}`. |
| `sql?` | `SqlAnswer` | Rows every `ctx.sql` returns, or a function given the statement (`$1…$n`) and its values. |
| `db?` | `unknown` | Handed to widgets as `ctx.db`. Default: `null`. |
| `session?` | `Session \| null` | Default: `null`. |
| `role?` | `string` | The role access checks compare. Default: `"admin"`. |
| `formatting?` | `FormattingConfig` | Without `admin`: locale, zone and currency, as `defineAdmin` takes them. |
| `labels?` | `LabelsConfig` | Without `admin`: overrides of the admin's strings. |
| `paths?` | `{ admin?: string }` | Without `admin`: where the admin is mounted, as `defineAdmin` takes `paths`. Default: ``{ admin: "/admin" }``. |

`headerContext` builds the second argument of `detail.title`, `subtitle` and
`badge`:

```ts excerpt
import { headerContext } from "@flowpanel/test/widgets";
import admin from "@/admin/config";

const ctx = headerContext({ admin });
expect(customers.options.detail?.title?.(row, ctx)).toBe("Northwind Audio");
```

`@flowpanel/test/widgets` is ESM-only.

#### Run it in Vitest

Inline FlowPanel's packages, or the run fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for
`next/cache`, and alias `@/`, since Vitest does not read `tsconfig.json` paths:

```ts excerpt
// vitest.config.ts
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";

export default defineConfig({
  resolve: { alias: { "@": fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url)) } },
  test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/@flowpanel\//] } } },
});
```

### Playwright config

`smokeAdmin` calls `page.goto(paths.admin)`, so set a `baseURL` and a `webServer`:

```ts excerpt
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  use: { baseURL: "http://localhost:3000" },
  webServer: { command: "pnpm dev", url: "http://localhost:3000", reuseExistingServer: true },
});
```

The test user needs the role your admin requires.

### Authentication

`cookie` suits a bare session token your own code issues. For better-auth,
next-auth and other providers that sign sessions, sign in first; `smokeAdmin` reuses
the page's context.

```ts excerpt
import { smokeAdmin } from "@flowpanel/test";

await page.goto("/login");
await page.getByLabel("Email").fill("admin@example.com");
await page.getByLabel("Password").fill(process.env.E2E_PASSWORD ?? "");
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }).click();

await smokeAdmin(page);
```

## ESLint plugin

Five rules that catch config mistakes the type system cannot.

Docs: https://flowpanel.tech/docs/reference/eslint-plugin

`@flowpanel/eslint-plugin` is an optional package that catches mistakes type-checking
misses: server code imported into a client component, a destructive action without
a confirm, duplicate resource names. Rule names are stable; options and messages
may change before 1.0.

### Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @flowpanel/eslint-plugin
```

It needs `eslint >= 8`; the config is flat config.

### Setup

```ts excerpt
import flowpanel from "@flowpanel/eslint-plugin";

export default [flowpanel.configs.recommended];
```

`configs.recommended` turns on all five rules. To choose them yourself:

```ts excerpt
import flowpanel from "@flowpanel/eslint-plugin";

export default [
  {
    plugins: { flowpanel },
    rules: {
      "flowpanel/prefer-shorthand-filter": "warn",
      "flowpanel/audit-row-action-needs-confirm": "error",
      "flowpanel/no-server-import-in-client": "error",
      "flowpanel/require-unique-resource-names": "error",
      "flowpanel/no-typo-column-keyword": "warn",
    },
  },
];
```

### The rules

| Rule | Recommended | Type | Fixable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`no-server-import-in-client`](#no-server-import-in-client) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`audit-row-action-needs-confirm`](#audit-row-action-needs-confirm) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`require-unique-resource-names`](#require-unique-resource-names) | `error` | problem | no |
| [`prefer-shorthand-filter`](#prefer-shorthand-filter) | `warn` | suggestion | yes |
| [`no-typo-column-keyword`](#no-typo-column-keyword) | `warn` | problem | no |

#### `no-server-import-in-client`

In a `"use client"` file, flags imports of:

- `server-only` and any `*/server-only` specifier;
- any specifier with a `/server` segment, such as `@/server/lib/auth` or
  `react-dom/server`, except `next/server`;
- an app-local path (`@/`, `~/`, `./`, `../`, `src/`) with a `db` segment, such as
  `@/db` or `../lib/db/client`.

`import type` is ignored.

#### `audit-row-action-needs-confirm`

Flags an `actions` or `bulkActions` entry with `variant: "destructive"` and no
`confirm`.

```ts excerpt
// bad
actions: [{ key: "delete", label: "Delete", variant: "destructive", run }];

// good
actions: [
  {
    key: "delete",
    label: "Delete",
    variant: "destructive",
    confirm: "Are you sure?",
    run,
  },
];
```

#### `require-unique-resource-names`

Flags two `resource()` entries in one `defineAdmin` with the same name, read from a
literal `options.name` or a string ref. Identifiers resolve through a
`const x = resource(…)` in the same file; the same unresolved identifier listed
twice is flagged too.

#### `prefer-shorthand-filter`

Rewrites filter `options` whose every `label` equals its `value` as plain strings.
Autofixable.

```ts excerpt
// bad
filters: [
  {
    field: "status",
    type: "select",
    options: [
      { label: "active", value: "active" },
      { label: "archived", value: "archived" },
    ],
  },
];

// good
filters: [{ field: "status", type: "select", options: ["active", "archived"] }];
```

#### `no-typo-column-keyword`

Flags `userid`, `createdat`, `updatedat` and `isactive`, in any casing other than
the camelCase one, in `columns`. The rule reads the source only, so it also catches
them where the rows are untyped. Not autofixable.
